minutes.headline: Water commissioners leaned toward a one-year rate-forecasting subscription but asked for reference checks first; no vote.
minutes.summary: The board assigned readings for Saturday's annual meeting articles, heard that the Keyes pilot test showed good PFAS breakthrough results but PFAS in the backwash and media plugging, and discussed a rate-management software proposal at length. They also reviewed a Woodlands zone one letter, a critical drought notice, a failed grant application, and a delinquent-bill dispute at Butterfly Lane. Formal motions were limited to minutes and adjournment.

what_happened.line: The Water District board took no vote on a rate-forecasting software subscription; members favored a one-year trial and asked for reference checks first.
The board heard that the Keyes PFAS pilot test showed good breakthrough results, with PFAS in the backwash and plugging of the filter media.
The district's water efficiency grant application was not funded, and the board said it will hold the meter on a delinquent Butterfly Lane account pending a payment arrangement.
Readers were assigned for the annual meeting articles, and the Woodlands zone one letter was received with no further response.
The only formal motions were on minutes and adjournment.

why_it_matters: The software subscription is not in the budget and would be paid from the system upgrades line, so it competes with infrastructure money that ratepayers fund through water bills.
The Keyes PFAS results and the wells being offline bear on water quality and on what treatment may cost, which is a likely driver of future rates.
The annual meeting articles are what residents will be asked to vote on at Saturday's meeting.
watch_next: The annual meeting on Saturday, where the assigned articles are read and voted.
Reference-town checks on the rate software, after which the board is expected to decide on the subscription.
